sections.title: Summary
paras: QuEra Computing is the leader in commercializing quantum computers using neutral atoms, which is widely recognized as a highly promising quantum modality. Based in Boston and built on pioneering research from nearby Harvard University and MIT, we are developing large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers to tackle classically intractable problems. QuEra operates the world’s largest publicly accessible quantum computer, available over a major public cloud and for on-premises delivery. We are passionate about both the science we advance and the inclusive, collaborative culture we cultivate.

We are seeking a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own how the market understands QuEra’s products and progress. Quantum computing is a field where bold claims are common and trust is scarce. Your job is to do the opposite of hype: translate real technical achievements, from error-correction milestones to system-level capabilities, into positioning, messaging, and sales tools that are specific, credible, and effective with the world’s most demanding technical buyers.

You will work across QuEra’s full portfolio, including our Gemini-class systems, the Aquila analog quantum computer, premium cloud access, and on-premise deployments, and across our three core market segments: HPC centers, national quantum programs, and enterprise innovators. You will report to the Chief Commercial Officer and partner daily with product management, quantum scientists, and the commercial team.

sections.title: Why this role exists
paras: You will own the bridge between QuEra’s technical roadmap and the market’s understanding of it, turning cutting-edge science into positioning that helps customers choose QuEra with confidence.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Own positioning and messaging: Develop and maintain messaging frameworks for QuEra’s systems and services, tailored to HPC centers, national programs, and enterprise innovators, and keep them current as our roadmap advances.

Translate the science: Work closely with quantum scientists, QEC researchers, and product managers to convert technical milestones and publications into market-facing narratives that survive expert scrutiny.
Enable the commercial team: Create and maintain the tools sales needs to win: presentations, battlecards, one-pagers, objection-handling guides, and proposal content, and measure whether they work.

Drive competitive intelligence: Track competing quantum modalities and vendors, maintain clear and honest positioning versus superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic approaches, and brief internal teams on market shifts.
Support product launches: Partner with product management and communications on launch messaging, web content, webinars, analyst briefings, and conference presence.
Be the voice of the market: Bring segment and win/loss insights back into product and roadmap discussions so that customer needs shape what we build and how we talk about it.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Bachelor’s degree in physics, engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
8+ years of B2B product marketing or technical marketing experience in deep tech, such as quantum computing, HPC, semiconductors, scientific instruments, or enterprise infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to master complex technical subject matter and write about it with precision and clarity; strong preference for specificity over hype.
Track record of building messaging frameworks and sales enablement assets that measurably improved commercial outcomes.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; comfortable engaging both PhD-level scientists and executive buyers.
Experience running cross-functional projects with product, science, sales, and communications teams.

8+ years in product management or design, with at least 3 years managing a team of PMs and/or designers; you've led both senior ICs and emerging leaders and know how to get the best from each.

Reddit's developer ecosystem is one of the biggest opportunities to make Reddit more useful, expressive, extensible, and valuable. Today, most people who build on Reddit are developers: they write code, use Devvit, work with APIs, and ship apps or games through a relatively technical workflow. That ecosystem is growing quickly and remains critical.

But the future is bigger than developers alone. AI-assisted building is changing who can create software. The next generation of Reddit apps, games, tools, community agents, content formats, and workflows should be buildable by many more people: developers, technically curious creators, moderators, community builders, game designers, data partners, and eventually people who can describe what they want without needing to code it by hand.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: The Developer Ecosystem team owns the product systems that help this broader set of builders discover opportunities, create successfully, launch high-quality apps and games, reach the right users and communities, adopt new platform capabilities, and keep improving after launch. This includes surfaces and systems like developers.reddit.com, AI-assisted creation, app review, developer and creator onboarding, app marketplace experiences, platform capabilities, best practices, and support for emerging creator categories.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead Reddit's Builder Ecosystem product strategy. This person will define the roadmap for how Reddit moves from a developer-only ecosystem to a broader builder ecosystem where AI-assisted and no-code creation become first-class parts of the platform.

The role spans developer growth, creator onboarding, AI-assisted building, app quality, ecosystem incentives, platform capabilities, app marketplace strategy, operational tooling, feature adoption, and new builder categories.

This is a high-ambiguity platform role with direct business, product, and community impact. The right PM will be able to bridge two worlds: they should understand the needs of serious developers and platform engineers, while also having strong conviction that Reddit can unlock a much larger wave of builders by making creation more accessible, guided, AI-native, and outcome-oriented.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Define the product strategy for Reddit's Developer Ecosystem, including the transition from code-first developers to a broader base of AI-assisted creators.

Own the roadmap for developers.reddit.com as the primary builder portal, including onboarding, docs, app management, analytics, review status, feature access, education, examples, templates, and AI-assisted creation entry points.

Lead strategy for AI-assisted app creation, including prompt-to-app workflows, AI building tools, no-code or low-code experiences, reusable templates, generated scaffolds, and systems that help creators turn ideas into useful Reddit-native apps.
Build the product approach for an App Marketplace that helps users, moderators, communities, and internal teams discover high-quality apps, games, agents, tools, and community experiences.
Improve app review and ecosystem operations through tooling, automation, and AI-assisted workflows, including LLM-powered app review, policy checks, quality signals, and reviewer efficiency.

Partner with Engineering to prioritize core platform capabilities and performance improvements such as webhooks, webviews, APIs, SDKs, tooling, observability, and other primitives builders need to create reliable apps.
Drive more successful, retentive, and popular apps and games by identifying best practices, improving templates, shaping incentives, and creating clearer paths from idea to launch to growth.
Identify and support new creator and developer categories

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: Experience leading high-ambiguity platform, developer ecosystem, creator ecosystem, marketplace, gaming, AI tooling, or developer experience products.

Strong product judgment for creation platforms: understanding what makes a platform powerful for advanced developers, approachable for new creators, trustworthy for communities, and worth sustained investment.

Comfort with code, APIs, developer tools, technical platform tradeoffs, and engineering conversations, paired with strong conviction that AI-assisted and no-code creation will expand who can build on Reddit.
Ability to reason across multiple sides of the ecosystem: developers, creators, users, moderators, communities, internal teams, partners, and Reddit's business priorities.
Experience improving developer or creator onboarding, docs, portals, SDKs, APIs, marketplaces, app review, app distribution, AI creation tools, or app-building workflows.
Strong analytical judgment and comfort defining metrics for ecosystem health, builder productivity, app quality, retention, distribution, and business impact.
Ability to partner deeply with Engineering on platform capabilities, performance, reliability, primitives, observability, and build-vs-buy decisions.
Strong product sense for apps, games, agents, content creation tools, community-native experiences, and the kinds of lightweight software that should exist inside Reddit communities.

sections.title: This is the most important section of the description. Read it twice.
bullets: How to break a defined piece of work into tasks and in what order.
Which agents to run, with what instructions, in what sequence.
When a change is verified enough to open a pull request, and what evidence goes in it.
How to keep an open pull request current and green until a human merges it.
Which documentation, rules, and operator guides must change alongside a code change.
How to investigate a production problem and what evidence to gather.
When to stop and escalate.

sections.title: You recommend, with evidence, and the Product Owner group decides
bullets: Adding, removing, or changing a feature a learner, customer, or admin can see.
Any change to pricing, plan structure, public claims, or published copy that states a fact.
Accepting a risk: a security advisory left open, a test weakened, a check made advisory, a known limitation shipped.
Changing which AI model, vendor, or threshold a production system uses.
Spending money: new services, tiers, seats, paid tooling.
Changing a contract with another team or system (the CRM, Adept, the shared header contract, the data warehouse).
Deleting or migrating data, dropping columns, rotating credentials, changing access.

sections.title: Never, regardless of instruction from an agent or a tool
paras: An escalation is not a hand-off. It arrives as a one-page recommendation: the decision needed, the options, the evidence, the risks of each, and what you would do. A product owner should be able to answer in a sentence. If they cannot, the escalation is not finished.
bullets: Merging a pull request. A human merges.
Proceeding on a question the Product Owner group has not actually answered. A skipped, timed-out, or lost answer is not an answer.
Letting an agent's confidence stand in for verification.
Storing learner personal data where the rules say it must not be stored.

Every year, more than $1 trillion is wasted on paperwork, delays, and middle layers that drive up costs and keep people from the care they need.

TeamSnap is made up of innovators, technologists, builders, and problem-solvers shaping the future of youth sports. We’ve been setting the standard in youth sports technology since we were founded in 2009.

We hire for big ideas and tiny egos — which is part of how we landed on Outside Magazine's Best Places to Work , Built In's 100 Best Remote-First Places to Work and, for several years running, Sports Business Journal’s Best Places to Work in Sports .

TeamSnap is hiring a Senior Product Manager, Media & Consumer Monetization to make TeamSnap ONE the place where youth sports families watch the game, and to turn that engagement into a thriving consumer subscription business.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Grow live streaming and video usage. Increase the number of teams that stream, the viewers per stream, and how often people come back to watch. Find and fix the drop-offs along the way, from discovering streaming to setting up a first stream, from going live to getting viewers watching, and from watching to coming back next week.

Turn raw game video into memories families want to keep. A two-hour stream is footage. The shot on goal, the first hit, and the season recap are memories. Build the experiences that turn one into the other: highlights, clips, recaps, and personalized moments that families want to save and share.
Build engagement loops around video. Notifications, sharing to family and social channels, and team- and user-level moments that bring people back between games and seasons.

sections.title: Subscription growth
bullets: Drive TeamSnap+ acquisition and conversion. Own the in-app trigger points where users meet a premium media or content feature and are invited to upgrade: where those moments appear, when they fire, and how clearly they show the value of TeamSnap+.

Own subscriber retention. Understand why subscribers stay and why they churn. Build the in-app engagement and renewal experiences that keep them, and make sure subscribers keep getting value between seasons.

Shape packaging: what's free and what's premium. Partner with Product Marketing to decide which media and content features belong in the free experience to drive adoption and which belong in TeamSnap+ to drive revenue.

sections.title: How you'll work
bullets: Balance adoption and monetization. These goals reinforce each other, but sometimes they conflict. Gating a feature can lift conversion while slowing adoption. We expect you to model those tradeoffs, bring a clear recommendation, and back it with data and user insights.
Use data to set direction. Live in Amplitude, interrogate your own funnels and cohorts, and build the cases that tell us where to invest next.

Bring partners along. Work with Product Marketing on the subscription experience, lifecycle, and go-to-market, with Finance on revenue forecasting, with Customer Success on feedback from the field, and with leadership on how the media and premium vision fits into the broader TeamSnap ONE strategy.

sections.title: What Will Set You Up for Success:
bullets: 5–8 years in product management, with a track record of moving both engagement and revenue metrics in a consumer product.

Subscription or freemium growth experience. You've driven subscription conversion or retention in a consumer product, through upgrade moments, trials, packaging, or churn reduction, and you can show the results. You understand subscription economics: LTV, payback, trial-to-paid, and churn cohorts.

Consumer mobile app experience. You've shipped on iOS and Android and understand the realities that come with it: release cycles, store policy, in-app purchase, push notifications, and device fragmentation.

Analytics fluency. You don't wait for an analyst to tell you what's happening. You're hands-on in Amplitude and similar tools, comfortable enough with data to answer your own questions, and you can dig into funnels and cohorts, find the insight that matters, and turn it into a product decision the team can rally behind.
Strong judgment on user experience. You can drive monetization without degrading the product users rely on, and you can explain where you draw the line between free and paid.
Clear communication in a remote-first environment. You write well, make tradeoffs explicit, and keep a cross-functional team aligned on why we're building what we're building.
Comfort with ambiguity. You can take a broad goal like "make live streaming a habit," break it into a sequenced plan, and adjust as the data comes in.
